current.text: He is Minnesota's clear backup center behind Rudy Gobert. Naz Reid and Julius Randle were traded away.
Minnesota has very thin big man depth. The only bigs are Gobert, Beringer, Lyles, Freeman and Rocco Zikarsky, and the team may start three guards.
He is projected for about 18 minutes a night off the bench. That is 10 to 11 more minutes than last season, a figure pulled back after the Kuminga signing.
He has no real path to starting. He is not expected to play power forward next to Gobert early in the season, but that could change as the year goes on.
One expert says he may not be ready for the backup center role.
His value depends on a Gobert injury. If Gobert misses games, he would start and be a must-roster player.
In reserve minutes he is a low-end blocks and FG% player. He can probably average about 1.1 blocks.
Taking him in round 11 of a 12-team standard league is an overdraft. Draft him only as a stash in best ball, weekly, games cap or deep bench formats.
With a March 28 end, Minnesota plays 4, 2 and 4 games in the fantasy playoffs. That puts a two-game week in the semifinal. The team has the league minimum of 13 back-to-backs.

durable.text: He is a great shot blocker and a strong, instinctive offensive rebounder. His defensive rebounding technique is behind.
He does not stretch the floor and makes almost no threes. He shoots free throws around 70%.
Foul trouble is a concern for him.
His category profile is high FG% on low volume, few turnovers and some blocks. Threes, assists and points are weak, and he projects to poor steals.
Experts see him as a future NBA starter and a possible top 50 fantasy player. In 28 minutes he could put up 12 points, 10 rebounds and 2.4 blocks on 60% shooting.

note: At Yahoo rank 182 and 0 USD on both Yahoo and ESPN, he falls outside our 144-player draft and should not be bought, even for 1 USD. As a backup he adds little beyond FG%, blocks and few turnovers (projected 1.0 BLK in about 18 minutes), and Minnesota has a two-game semifinal week. Leave him on waivers and watch Gobert's health early in the season: if Gobert misses time, Beringer becomes a must add for blocks, rebounds and FG%.
